name: Frill
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Publish feedback, roadmap, and announcements for one product

tiers.name: Startup
tiers.limits: 50 active ideas; 1 survey of each supported type; unlimited admins, widgets and tracked users.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited ideas; 3 surveys of each supported type; unlimited admins, widgets and tracked users.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Unlimited ideas and surveys; Privacy, Surveys and White Labeling included.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited ideas and surveys; SOC 2 controls, audit log, IP allowlisting and dedicated support.

pricing.billingTerms: Monthly + annual; exact annual-equivalent rates were not exposed on the checked page. A 14-day trial is offered without a card.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Privacy, Surveys and White Labeling are paid add-ons on lower tiers; their individual prices were not publicly stated.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Frill, publish feedback, roadmap, and announcements for one product. The hard boundary is hosted polish, custom domain, integrations, widgets, and simple pricing, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Collect structured feedback for one product, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a roadmap, announcements, and a transparent status view.
whatYouLose: hosted polish, custom domain, integrations, widgets, and simple pricing
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Frill because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: ClearFlask
alternatives.desc: A mature open-source feedback loop; the AWS-shaped deployment is the punchline.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with the project's bundled dependencies
facts.dataFormat: In a self-hosted deployment the source-of-truth records live in a DynamoDB-compatible store, search/filter indexes live in MySQL/MariaDB or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, and uploads live in S3-compatible storage; the bundled Compose profile persists these services under the deployment's data directory. The hosted edition keeps the equivalent data in ClearFlask's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: ClearFlask can publish feedback and roadmaps, but deploying its database, search, storage, email, and proxy stack is wildly more work than Frill's focused hosted product.
facts.setupBlocker: The simple Compose command starts a large dependency stack; a public deployment still needs environment configuration, a domain/TLS, outbound email, backups, and several stateful services.

alternatives.name: Quackback
alternatives.desc: Feedback, roadmap and changelog in one self-hosted stack, with no per-user invoice.

facts.dataFormat: Feedback posts, votes, comments, users, roadmap items, and changelog entries live in the deployment's PostgreSQL database; uploaded assets and generated files remain in the Docker-hosted storage configured by the deployment.
facts.gapVsPaid: Quackback covers feedback, roadmap, and changelog, but the owner assumes hosting and upgrades and gets a younger, less integrated product than Frill.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must supply environment secrets, run and update Docker Compose, expose the service behind HTTPS, configure email, and back up its database.

alternatives.name: Sleekplan Indie
alternatives.desc: The whole feedback-roadmap-changelog loop for one admin, permanently free and visibly branded.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then embed the widget or publish the hosted feedback portal
facts.dataFormat: Feedback, votes, comments, roadmap items, changelog posts, user records, and widget configuration live in Sleekplan's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sleekplan Indie is close functionally, but one administrator, vendor branding, and paid-only workflow and customization controls limit it as the product or team grows.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no technical install hurdle, but the free Indie plan is limited to one administrator, carries Sleekplan branding, and reserves deeper workflow and customization controls for paid plans.

alternatives.name: UserJot
alternatives.desc: Feedback, roadmap and announcements on one free plan, with unlimited users and two boards.

facts.install: Hosted signup, create a board, and optionally add the widget or identify users
facts.dataFormat: Feedback, votes, comments, statuses, roadmap and changelog entries, user identity data, and configuration live in UserJot's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: UserJot's free plan covers the loop but stops at two boards and offers a smaller integration, customization, and support surface than Frill.
facts.setupBlocker: Setup is clean, but the permanent free plan is bounded to two boards and omits paid branding, domain, segmentation, and advanced administration options.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Startup plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Frill in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect structured feedback for one product, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a roadmap, announcements, and a transparent status view.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
